articles.title: Hogh and Tierney close to returns for Celtic
articles.summary: Manager Martin O'Neill confirms Celtic duo Kasper Hogh and Kieran Tierney could play a part in Wednesday's Scottish Premiership match at St Johnstone.
body: Denmark striker Hogh, who became the Scottish champions' record signing this summer, has not played since the second leg of Celtic's Champions League play-off defeat against LASK on 25 August.
"We've had Kasper back the last couple of days and Kieran did a little bit of work with us [on Tuesday] morning, so we'll have a look to see how they are," O'Neill said.
"We've got a couple of other fitness issues for players but we'll try and go as strong as we possibly can."
On whether he is hopeful Hogh and Tierney could play some part on Wednesday, O'Neill added: "Yeah, obviously Kasper's had the extra day, we'll see how they are [on Wednesday]."

articles.title: Najidi Storm earns unwelcome tag of shortest-priced loser in British racing history
articles.summary: Favourite beaten at odds of 1-33 at Goodwood. Bookies still claim they lost on outcome of race. His father is Frankel, the greatest horse that ever looked through a bridle.
body: But on Tuesday Najidi Storm forever brought ignominy and shame to his blue-blooded family when he became the shortest-priced loser in the history of British racing, beaten into second in the glamorously titled Cleansing Service Group Novice Stakes at Goodwood at odds of 1-33.

The aptly named Wreck It Ronnie won the contest at what now look like generous odds of 10-1 in a field of just three. The winner had been beaten a combined 22 and a half lengths in his only two previous outings, but made virtually all the running in the hands of Kieren Fox and no matter how hard jockey Lewis Edmunds tried he could not reel him in on the Harry Charlton-trained favourite.

The other runner in the 10-furlong event, Dream Of Albion, was a well tailed off 76 lengths back in arrears. The previous record was jointly held by Doom (2023) and Royal Forest (1948), who were both beaten at a starting price of 1-25.

Of course the bookmakers were still moaning, claiming they failed to make money after the shock outcome. Brian O’Keeffe of BOYLE Sports, said: “We’ve witnessed the shortest-priced loser in British racing history, but that doesn’t mean it was a good result for the layers.

articles.title: Premier League clubs face losing lucrative sponsors if unlicensed gambling firms banned
articles.summary: Ten clubs could lose tens of millions of pounds next year. Ladbrokes owner highlights PM’s position as Everton fan. Half of the Premier League’s 20 clubs have sponsorship or advertising deals with unlicensed gambling companies that could be illegal next year under plans being developed by the…
body: An eight-week consultation on proposals to ban sponsorship from gambling companies not licensed in the UK closes on Wednesday, with licensed operators such as Ladbrokes and William Hill pitted against the Premier League in a battle that could cost clubs tens of millions of pounds.

The league is understood to be lobbying against a ban on the grounds that the services offered by primarily Asia-facing betting companies and online casinos are not available in the UK, although anyone with a VPN can open an account and place a bet in minutes.
Analysis conducted by the Guardian has found the number of top-flight clubs who have commercial relationships with unlicensed operators has risen from six to 10 over the summer.
The increase is likely to have been influenced by the league’s decision to impose a voluntary ban from this season on front-of-shirt sponsorship deals with gambling companies.

articles.title: England different from when Pietersen left - Root
articles.summary: Joe Root says the England team is "very different" to the one Kevin Pietersen was sacked from in 2014, after the former batter joined the coaching staff of the white-ball side.
body: Captain Root is the only remaining England Test player to have been in the same team as Pietersen and was on the Ashes tour of 2013-14 that signalled the end of the 46-year-old's international career.
On Monday it was announced that Pietersen will join the white-ball team as a mentor in the build-up to the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, the country of his birth.
"I'm fortunate enough to be in that position where I did play alongside him," Root told BBC Sport.
"A lot of the guys will have watched him and got into the game because of him. It will be great for those guys to have the opportunity to work alongside him."

articles.title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule
articles.summary: Legal action from the top European leagues and global players' union Fifpro against Fifa is extended to include the world governing body's "abusive conduct" towards the women's game.
body: European Leagues, which represents 53 professional divisions, including the Premier League, and 1,328 clubs in 34 countries, first filed the complaint to the European Commission to protect the welfare of men's players in October 2024.

The complaint stated that Fifa abused a dominant position under European competition law allegedly by not including national leagues and player unions over the new men's international calendar announced in 2023.

In a statement on Tuesday, it said it is extending the scope of its complaint to include "Fifa's abusive conduct regarding the women's international match calendar and related women's football regulatory decisions".
"Fifa's conduct threatens the growth and financial sustainability of women's professional leagues, and risks player health and wellbeing," European Leagues said.

articles.title: Ferrari vow to come back stronger after Monza 'failure'
articles.summary: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says his team will head to this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid with "all the energy" to bounce back from their "failure" at Monza.
body: There were big expectations for Ferrari at their home event after Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were quick in Friday practice, only to miss out on the front row in qualifying before a dismal race on Sunday.
Hamilton dropped from fourth to 10th after going side by side with Leclerc at the first chicane, going through the gravel at Turn 2, which he was unhappy with.
Then Leclerc had a huge crash on the third lap which wrecked the car and left the Monegasque driver with initial eye issues.
Hamilton was up to third at one point in the race but lacked outright pace and finished sixth behind both Mercedes, Red Bull's Max Verstappen and both McLarens.

articles.title: Man Utd's £1bn rebuild faces toughest test
articles.summary: Michael Carrick transformed Manchester United's fortunes after his appointment in January, steering the side from seventh to third and clinching their return to the Champions League.
body: But, after a disappointing start to the new campaign, how will they handle the challenge of juggling three games per week? And has their rebuild neglected one key part of their squad?
With no European football and early exits from the Carabao Cup and FA Cup against Grimsby Town and Brighton respectively, Manchester United only played 40 games in all competitions last term.
It was the joint-fewest of any Premier League side and the club's lowest total for a single season since the 1913/14 campaign.

The light schedule allowed Carrick to keep key players fresh while Manchester United's rivals were having to rotate. In the period between his appointment and the conclusion of the Premier League season, only five sides made fewer line-up changes than United.

articles.title: Mac Allister 'very sad' over no new Liverpool deal
articles.summary: Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister is "very sad" that he has not been offered a new contract and admitted he had "options to leave" in the summer.
body: The 27-year-old confirmed he has two years left on his Reds deal, which he signed when he joined the club in the summer of 2023.
The Argentina international's unhappiness comes after fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch penned new long-term contracts this year.
Speaking ahead of Liverpool's Champions League opener against Atletico Madrid, Mac Allister told a pre-match press conference: "There was a chance [he could have left the club in the summer].
"As everyone knows, I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which makes me very, very sad.
